lab_table.hypothesis: Misses concentrate in the small size tertile for every class, so shrinking paste scale to 0.3-0.7 (covering the 25-60px missed range) should raise small-instance recall and mAP. Confirmed if inclusion AP50 jumps well above 0.18 and low-tertile recall improves vs control; if flat, scale is not the lever.

Inclusion's low AP50 (0.18) may be data scarcity (10 real images) rather than scale. Doubling its allocation (25/12/13) at the default scale should lift inclusion AP without hurting the other classes. Confirmed if inclusion AP50 rises more than in candidate 1/control while patches/scratches hold.

Scratches have the highest FP rate (0.22/img) and low-contrast instances are missed everywhere; pasting onto any_class backgrounds adds texture diversity and co-occurring defects, improving precision/robustness. Confirmed if precision (esp. scratches) improves vs control without recall loss.
CONTROL (added by the lab): default generation recipe, balanced allocation.

lesson: Small paste scale (0.3-0.7) is the dominant lever: best mAP50 (0.604) and best patches AP50 (0.79), confirming the small-miss hypothesis. Balanced allocation beat inclusion-heavy, and any_class backgrounds badly hurt inclusion (0.21) — keep same_class + balanced + small scale. Next round: build on small scale and probe whether going even smaller (0.3-0.5) or prefer_small sources recovers the still-missed smallest instances, while keeping same_class pool.
